# Evaluation independence (generated by `scripts/check_eval_independence.py`)

## Provenance of the 186 knowledge-base outcome rows

| source file | rows | seed range |
|---|---|---|
| `results/benchmark-v1/benchmark_raw.jsonl` | 150 | 100-145 |
| `results/benchmark-v2/rerun/benchmark_v2_evaluated.jsonl` | 36 | 202-424 |

Policy per row: ['benchmark-system-v1 policy (equivalent to rulebooks/benchmark-v2.yaml)', 'benchmark-system-v2 policy (rulebooks/benchmark-v2.yaml)'].
Each row is one benchmark run of a supported fault scenario: the first action executed on the injected service, the run's self-verified recovery, the load generator's failed-request percentage and the recovery time.

## Overlap with evaluation v3 (seeds 600-649, scenarios crash, latency, error_spike, memory_leak, disk_fill, bad_deploy, cpu_burn, traffic_surge, good_deploy)

| data that built or selected something | description | seeds shared with v3 |
|---|---|---|
| knowledge-base measured outcomes (fix ranking) | 186 rows from 2 files | none |
| classifier, ranker, detectors (training runs) | 105 no-action live runs (training seeds 1000-1707 and 1800-1842, 1 corrupted runs excluded), scenarios ['bad_deploy', 'c | none |
| root margin 0.1215 (out-of-fold training incidents) | 316 incidents from the same training runs | none |

## What this means
- **No run is shared:** no v3 seed was used to build the knowledge base, train any model, or choose any threshold.
- **Not a held-out system or a held-out fault family:** v3 runs the same application, the same nine scripted scenarios and the same injection code as the benchmarks whose outcomes ranked the fixes (v1, v2) and as the training runs. The fix order the brain uses was chosen with v1/v2 outcomes of these same scenarios.
- So v3 is fresh-seed evidence on the same scenario families: new runs, not new conditions. It is not evidence of generalisation to other applications or fault types (the dataset-A experiment and the RCAEval experiments address that, separately and offline).
- With the committed knowledge base, the ranking did not change any proposed (first) runbook (`tests/test_kb.py`). For v3 the proposals are therefore the same as the fixed table's, and the v1/v2 outcomes influenced only the order of the lower alternatives.
